newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says mineral water label not tied to health.
newsitem.headline: Court says mineral water label not tied to health.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday member states cannot require vendors of bottled water to first prove that water labelled as natural mineral water actually promotes good health.
The court's judgment challenges German law which requires that before water can be labeled as "natural mineral water" it must contain minerals and trace elements demonstrated to improve health.
German law does not characterize water as natural mineral water simply because it is low in sodium and chlorine.

The court's review of the Community directive on the exploitation and marketing of mineral water revealed no explicit reference in the definition of such water to "properties favourable to health", and noted the final version removed such language originally proposed by the Commission.
"This suggests the Council did not intend to make recognition of water as natural mineral water dependent on its possessing properties favourable to health," the court said.
Reference for a preliminary ruling from the Bundesverwaltungsgericht in the proceedings pending before that court between
on the interpretation of Council directive 80/777/EEC on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the exploitation and marketing of natural mineral waters (OJ 1980 L 229, p. 1)

Article 1(1) of Council directive 80/777/EEC on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the expolitation and marketing of natural mineral waters, in conjunction with Annex I, Section I, paragraphs 1 and 2 thereto, must be interpreted as precluding a member state from making the recognition of water as natural mineral water dependent on its possessing properties favourable to health.
